gaps.problem: No free judge-backed sheet tests EXPLAIN reading, index selection or plan forcing — LeetCode and HackerRank grade output, not plans. This module stays synthesised.
gaps.fill: Keep the synthesised drills as the primary source here; grade against a seeded local Postgres by plan shape rather than result set. Reference: Use The Index, Luke (https://use-the-index-luke.com/).

gaps.problem: Gap filling, interpolation, PostGIS and H3 appear in no mainstream interview sheet. Advanced time-series/spatial work is deliberately off-spine.
gaps.fill: PGExercises Date x6 covers calendar arithmetic now. Extended spatial and missing-data material stays synthesised against a seeded Postgres + PostGIS.

gaps.problem: Sourced coverage is thin — 6 date-arithmetic problems from PGExercises L2 only.
gaps.fill: PGExercises date section adds timetable realism; DataLemur Hard-graded analytics fill the numeric side. Do not force a spatial sheet that does not exist.

gaps.problem: Recursive CTEs are absent from SQL 50 and near-absent from HackerRank; they now carry 2 sourced rows (LC1270, LC1767) plus synthesised drills.
gaps.fill: Advanced SQL 50 supplies 2 recursive problems; PGExercises Recursive is the natural follow-up if a third source is ever needed.

gaps.problem: L4 has 6 sourced problems across the whole bank (X4 x3 HR, W4 x1 LC, S4 x2 LC). L4 stays constraint-driven and internals-heavy by design.
gaps.fill: Do not force more L4 sourcing. Synthesised drills remain primary at L4.

rules: A sourced problem is never invented. Every entry carries platform + ref + url, or it does not go in this file.
tier is assigned by THIS curriculum, not by the platform's difficulty label. difficulty is recorded as provenance only.
The spine fixes order. An overlay may add reps at a tier but may not introduce a concept ahead of the spine.
A module's lesson may cite a sourced problem only if problems.json lists it for that module at that tier.
Synthesised drills stay legal and stay in the lesson files, but must be labelled platform='drill' so the origin is never ambiguous.
